subject: Private deployment — exit-channel callbacks, IP allowlist & firewall constraints
messages:
From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@medsys-health.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@medsys-health.com>
Date: 2025-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — control-plane callbacks and egress constraints

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Per our security team we need to lock down outbound connectivity for the private deployment of Redwood in our VPC. Two specific asks we need formal guidance on before we proceed with procurement: 

1) Control-plane callbacks: your hosted control plane will initiate status/call-home traffic (health checks, metrics upload, rollout signals). We need the exact destination FQDNs and an expected set of TLS SNI values to allow through the perimeter. Short-lived IPs are acceptable only if you provide a signed list or an allowlist-synchronization endpoint.

2) Egress identity: we cannot allow arbitrary egress through a NAT for the private runtime. We prefer either a static set of IPs per-customer, a small pool per-region mapped to our tenant, or an mTLS-authenticated egress proxy that validates client certs.

Attached is our internal tunnel/egress policy (medsys-egress-requirements.pdf) — please review and confirm which model Redwood supports, plus any firewall ACL snippets we can hand to our infra team.

We'd like to resolve this before EoM procurement signoff.

Best,
Alex
Network Architect, MedSys Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@medsys-health.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@medsys-health.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — control-plane callbacks and egress constraints

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the PDF. High level answers up front so you can share with procurement/security: 

- We support per-tenant static egress IPs for Dedicated/Private customers in the US regions (recommended for strict allowlists). For on-prem VMs we can negotiate a small, reserved IP block assigned to your control-plane-facing egress gateway.
- Where static IPs are not possible, we offer an allowlist-sync endpoint (HTTPS, token-auth) and a signed JSON manifest that contains verifiable IP allocations and a signature you can validate.
- Control-plane callbacks use mTLS on a set of canonical hostnames (control.redwood-inference.com and metrics.redwood-inference.com) and present an SNI matching the hostname; we will provide our CA bundle for cert validation.

Attached is a short firewall snippet with recommended CIDR and port/host entries (redwood-proposed-fw-snippets.txt). It contains two modes: STATIC_IPS and SYNC_MANIFEST.

Action items I propose: 
- Kimberly (cc) to confirm compliance constraints around signed manifests and CA pinning.
- Alex/Priya to confirm which model (STATIC_IPS vs SYNC_MANIFEST) your infra prefers.
- I'll follow up with a scoped draft that lists expected IP ranges and rotation cadence.

If helpful we can also run a short on-call test where we perform a simulated callback while your fw team watches logs.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Technical Account Lead — Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood-proposed-fw-snippets.txt)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Soto <alex.soto@medsys-health.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@medsys-health.com>
Date: 2025-05-18T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — control-plane callbacks and egress constraints

Marcus/Alex — quick compliance checks and clarifications from our side: 

- Signed manifest approach is acceptable from an evidence standpoint provided the manifest uses a SHA256 signature with a rotating signing key and we publish the public keys via a stable URL with versioning. That meets auditability requirements.
- Per-tenancy static IPs are preferred for customers who need short retention and minimal outbound surface; note these IPs will be advertised from our egress pool and will rotate on planned windows (we commit to 90 days notice for IP changes).
- mTLS is required for control-plane endpoints that accept configuration changes or rollout commands. For telemetry and non-privileged metrics uploads we support mutual TLS or token-based TLS depending on the customer's choice.

Two compliance asks for your infra team to sign off: 
1) Please confirm whether your firewall can perform SNI-based allowlisting (some appliances only allow FQDNs for HTTP and not for arbitrary TLS flows). If not, we'll need to provide IPs instead.
2) If you choose SYNC_MANIFEST, ensure your firewall can fetch manifests on a scheduled basis (we recommend 5-minute interval) and apply diffs atomically to avoid transient blackholes.

I'll prepare a short runbook for auditors showing how signed manifests are verified and logged (we'll include timestamps, signature verification, and manifest version).

Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@medsys-health.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-19T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — control-plane callbacks and egress constraints

Alex/Priya — short note from the account team: agreed path forward is to provision STATIC_IPS for your first rollout so procurement can complete with a deterministic allowlist. Marcus — please provide the initial static /29 block list and our expected rotation windows by EOD Monday (2025-05-26).

If MedSys later wants to move to SYNC_MANIFEST for automated rotation, we will run a small pilot in staging. Per our compliance team we will deliver the manifest signing spec and the auditor runbook by next Wednesday.

Thanks all — Jordan Blake, Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
